data.one_liner: Mixin and provider that expose RouteObserver callbacks like didPush and didPop for easy use.
data.what_it_does: It supplies a RouteObserverProvider and a RouteObserverMixin so widgets can listen to navigation events without boilerplate. The mixin forwards RouteAware callbacks and streams them via Provider/Riverpod.
use_when: You need to react to navigation events (push/pop) in a widget
You already use Provider or Riverpod and want a lightweight solution
You prefer a mixin rather than manual RouteObserver handling
avoid_when: You need a full routing solution with deep linking or nested routes
You rely on code‑generated route classes
You don't use Provider/Riverpod and prefer a pure Navigator API
strengths: Very small and easy to add
Works with both Provider and Riverpod
Provides stream‑based access to route events
weaknesses: Only covers route‑observer callbacks, no routing features
May clash if multiple RouteObservers are added
data.setup_notes: Wrap MaterialApp with RouteObserverProvider (or use RouteObserverProvider widget) and add the mixin to your State class.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides full routing with generated routes and also supports route‑aware callbacks

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers declarative routing, deep linking and navigation guard features

data.minimal_example:
void main(){runApp(MultiProvider(providers:[RouteObserverProvider(),ChangeNotifierProvider(create:(_)=>Logger())],child:const App()));}

class App extends StatelessWidget{Widget build(BuildContext c){return MaterialApp(navigatorObservers:[RouteObserverProvider.of(c)],home:const APage());}}
